Lessons.Title: The Number $e$
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Comprehend that $e$ represents a constant whose value is approximately 2.718.
The constant e≈2.71828 is the base of natural logarithms and continuous exponential growth. It can be described by the limit (1+1/n)^n as n increases; it is not a variable.

Here are three representations of a function that models how the mold is growing. \(a(t) = 10 \boldcdot e^t\) What do you notice? What do you wonder? The highest interest rate is 100%, calculated once a year. The lower the interest rate, the more often it gets… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: The function \(f\) is given by \(f(x) = (1+x)^{\frac{1}{x}}\). How do the values of \(f\) behave for small positive and large positive values of \(x\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Since 1992, the value of homes in a neighborhood has doubled every 16 years. The value of one home in the neighborhood was $136,500 in 1992. What is the value of this home, in dollars, in the year 2000? Explain your reasoning. Write an equation that represents the growth in housing value as a function of time in \(t\)… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: Write two equations—one in exponential form and one in logarithmic form—to represent each question. Use “?” for the unknown value. “To what exponent do we raise the number 5 to get 625?” “What is the log, base 3, of 27?” Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 8: Clare says that \(\log 0.1 = \text-1\). Kiran says that \(\log (\text-10) = \text-1\). Do you agree with either one of them? Explain your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
